battle.name: 安提柯與納巴泰的對抗
battle.brief: 公元前312年，安提柯一世「獨眼」為掃清地中海東岸的商路，在阿拉伯邊境向納巴泰人開戰，攻其海陸門戶加沙；托勒密、塞琉古與安提柯之子德米特里聯軍前來解圍，卻在加沙附近的會戰中被安提柯擊潰。卡面科林斯青銅盔正出自這支部隊的裝備譜系：它只留兩條眼縫，戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 公元前312年的地中海東岸，是亞歷山大大帝帝國崩解後「繼業者」諸王爭奪的地帶，這場戰爭正開在它最南端的一條商路上。開戰的一方是安提柯一世「獨眼」：馬其頓人，亞歷山大的舊部，亞細亞與敘利亞的統治者，此時坐鎮安條克與腓尼基的港口，控制著呂基亞、弗里吉亞、小亞細亞東岸與黎凡特內陸，他的海軍由兒子德米特里率領。對手是納巴泰人：以阿拉伯沙漠為基地的部族聯盟，他們掌握的不是土地而是商路——從阿拉伯半島南部與厄多姆一帶通往地中海的乳香與香料路線，終點就在加沙，納巴泰人以駱駝隊與輕騎護送貨隊，在加沙一線設有據點與稅卡。第三方是托勒密一世與塞琉古一世：托勒密此時仍是埃及的總督，他與塞琉古在西敘利亞結盟，兩人合兵北上解加沙之圍，聯軍中還有安提柯的兒子德米特里。戰區北面，卡山德一系在博斯普魯斯與色雷斯方向牽制安提柯的西翼，使安提柯無法把全部兵力集中到一處。整個戰區可以分成南北兩條相咬的線：南線是安提柯的陸軍深入阿拉伯邊境，北線是德米特里的艦隊在塞浦路斯與黎凡特之間爭奪海上通道，兩條線的勝負最後在加沙一城的攻防上合流。
countriesEn: The eastern Mediterranean of 312 BC lay in the zone the successor kings were tearing apart after the collapse of the Alexander empire, and this war was fought on the southernmost stretch of its caravan roads. The party that opened the war was Antigonus I Monophthalmus, the One-Eyed: a Macedonian, an old companion of Alexander, ruler of Asia and Syria, based at Antioch and at the Phoenician ports, holding Lycia, Phrygia, the east coast of Asia Minor and the interior of the Levant, with his fleet under his son Demetrius. His opponent was the Nabataeans, a tribal confederation based in the Arabian desert, whose control lay not over territory but over the roads: the terminus of the incense and spice route that ran from southern Arabia and Edom down to the Mediterranean lay at Gaza, and the Nabataeans escorted their caravans with camel trains and light cavalry, holding posts and toll-stations on the Gaza line. The third party was Ptolemy I and Seleucus I: Ptolemy was still satrap of Egypt, and he had allied with Seleucus in western Syria; the two marched north together to relieve Gaza, and the coalition included Antigonus's own son Demetrius. On the northern front, the party of Cassander was tying down Antigonus's western wing around the Hellespont and Thrace, so that Antigonus could not concentrate all his strength on one point. The whole theatre can be seen as two lines biting into each other: a southern line where Antigonus's land army pushed into the Arabian frontier, and a northern line where Demetrius's fleet contested the sea lanes between Cyprus and the Levant. The two lines came together in the fighting over the single city of Gaza.
people: 這場戰爭留下姓名的多數是統帥。安提柯一世「獨眼」是馬其頓安提柯王朝的建立者，此時以亞細亞與敘利亞的主人自居，尚未正式稱王，但軍隊與實力已足以單獨對抗兩位總督；他的右眼是六年之後、公元前306年第二次圍攻加沙時才失明的，所以在公元前312年他仍是兩眼俱全。與他對面的納巴泰首領，古典史料沒有留下可以確定的名字：通行編年中最著名的納巴泰王阿雷塔斯三世屬於更晚的一代（通行年代約公元前282至前246年在位），不能套用到公元前312年。托勒密一世是托勒密王朝的奠基者，此時以埃及總督的身分在軍中；他的兄弟梅涅勞斯任海軍統帥，在公元前312年的塞浦路斯薩拉米斯海戰中戰敗被俘，隨後的加沙會戰裡又有托勒密本人出現在前線。塞琉古一世此時仍是被安提柯逐出東方的失勢者，東山再起全靠這一場戰役的消息；他在戰後回到美索不達米亞，此後再未回到地中海東岸作戰。安提柯的兒子德米特里這年二十出頭：他在塞浦路斯海戰中擊敗托勒密的艦隊，俘獲羅得島的海軍統帥阿拉托斯，加沙會戰中又獨當一翼，戰後因表現出色獲父親所賜的鍍金胸甲——這副胸甲日後在伊普索斯會戰中幾乎要了他的命。安提柯的另一員大將佩伊通奉命率援軍趕到，後來在東方成為塞琉古最難纏的對手之一。還要記住一點史料上的限度：以上一切都靠狄奧多羅斯《史學》第十五卷的摘要拼出，沒有第二個獨立來源可以互相印證，連「安提柯在沙漠內陸受挫」這種事，也只剩這一份孤證。
peopleEn: Most of the names that survive from this war belong to the commanders. Antigonus I Monophthalmus, the One-Eyed, founder of the Macedonian Antigonid dynasty, styled himself lord of Asia and Syria though not yet king, and his troops and resources already allowed him to face two satraps single-handed. His right eye was not lost until six years later, in 306 BC during the second siege of Gaza, so in 312 BC he was still two-eyed. The Nabataean chief on the other side has no securely identifiable name in the classical sources: the best-known Nabataean king, Aretas III, belongs to a later generation, with the conventional dates of his reign about 282-246 BC, and cannot be applied to 312 BC. Ptolemy I, founder of the Ptolemaic dynasty, was in the field in his capacity as satrap of Egypt; his brother Menelaus commanded the fleet and had been beaten and taken prisoner in the naval battle of Salamis in Cyprus in 312 BC, and Ptolemy himself was in the front line at the subsequent battle of Gaza. Seleucus I was at this moment the man whom Antigonus had driven out of the East, and his entire recovery rested on the news of this campaign; after the battle he returned to Mesopotamia and never campaigned on the eastern Mediterranean coast again. Antigonus's son Demetrius was in his early twenties: he had beaten Ptolemy's fleet at Salamis in Cyprus and taken the Rhodian admiral Aratus prisoner, and at Gaza he commanded a wing on his own; after the fight his father gave him a gilt breastplate for his conduct, and that breastplate was very nearly to kill him years later at Ipsus. Antigonus's other leading officer, Peithon, was ordered up with reinforcements and later became one of Seleucus's most awkward opponents in the East. One limit of the evidence should also be recorded: all of this is assembled from the epitome of Diodorus, and there is no second independent witness to check it against, so even the fact of Antigonus's setback in the desert interior rests on a single late summary.
kits: 卡面上那頂科林斯青銅盔，是這場戰爭裡最值得說明的一件裝備。科林斯盔約在公元前650年前後定型：青銅鑄成，殼形覆住整個頭顱，只留兩條水平眼縫與一道鼻脊開孔，護頰可以放下或上翻，戴上之後視線只剩一條窄縫。它原本是希臘城邦重裝步兵的制式裝備，配套的是大圓盾（aspis）、短劍（xiphos）與投槍（dory），用途只有一個：在正面對撞中用身體與盾牌的厚度硬吃對方的矛尖。公元前312年的安提柯軍中，這頂盔並不是馬其頓方陣的標準頭盔——此時的方陣仍用色雷斯式的輕盔配大圓盾。科林斯盔在那支軍隊裡會以兩種身分出現：一是僱兵與盟軍步兵的舊式裝備，在安提柯與托勒密、塞琉古雙方都還不少見；二是它的未來：安提柯在接下來十年裡改革方陣，把科林斯盔配上小圓盾（所謂「持盾者」的前排）與加長的方陣長矛，到公元前301年伊普索斯會戰時，這頂盔就成為安提柯方陣最認得出的標誌——那時安提柯正是在輸掉的那一仗裡把它用到極致。這場戰爭實際用過的其他兵器：馬其頓式方陣長矛與葉形矛頭、短劍與kopis式佩劍、希臘式圓盾（hoplon）與後來的小圓盾、弓與箭（安提柯的希臘式弓兵，以及托勒密由埃及弓兵與安納托利亞弓兵混成的遠射隊）、短投槍（akontion）與標槍；騎兵方面是馬其頓騎槍與小盾（kavadion）對上納巴泰人的駱駝騎兵與沙漠輕騎；攻城方面，加沙有城牆、塔樓與城壕，安提柯對加沙用的是封鎖海路、斷絕城郊水井的圍城法，史料沒有記錄使用攻城塔或撞槌；後勤方面，海運由腓尼基港口（推羅、西頓）供給，沙漠行軍靠水囊、駱駝馱隊與有限的水井，這也是安提柯必須先拿下加沙作為補給點的原因。
kitsEn: The Corinthian bronze helmet on the card is the piece of equipment in this war most worth explaining. The type was fixed by about 650 BC: cast in bronze, the shell covering the whole skull, leaving only two horizontal eye slits and the opening along the nasal ridge, with cheek-pieces that could be dropped or turned up, so that once it was on, the wearer's sight was reduced to a narrow slit. It was originally the standard kit of the heavy infantry of the Greek city-states, and went with the large round shield, the aspis, the short sword, the xiphos, and the thrusting spear, the dory; it had a single purpose, to take the enemy's spearhead on the thickness of the body and the shield in a frontal collision. In Antigonus's army of 312 BC this helmet was not the standard headgear of the Macedonian phalanx, which still wore the lighter Thracian helmet with the large round shield. The Corinthian helmet would appear in that army in two guises: first, as the old equipment of mercenary and allied infantry, still common on both Antigonus's side and that of Ptolemy and Seleucus; second, as its own future, for during the ten years after this Antigonus reformed his phalanx, pairing the Corinthian helmet with the small round shield worn by the shield-bearers of the front rank and with a lengthened phalanx spear, so that by the battle of Ipsus in 301 BC the helmet had become the most recognisable badge of the Antigonid phalanx, and Antigonus was using it to the limit in the very battle he lost. The other weapons actually present in this war: Macedonian phalanx spears with leaf-shaped heads, short swords and kopis blades worn at the side, Greek round shields, the hoplon, and later the smaller shield, bows and arrows, with Antigonus's Greek archers and the mixed Egyptian and Anatolian archers in Ptolemy's line, and short javelins, the akontion, as well as heavier darts. On the cavalry side, the Macedonian cavalry lance and small shield, the kavadion, faced the Nabataean camel cavalry and desert light horse. On siege matters, Gaza had walls, towers and a ditch, and Antigonus's siege of it was a blockade of the sea route combined with cutting off the wells outside the city; the sources record no use of siege towers or battering rams. On logistics, sea supply ran from the Phoenician ports, Tyre and Sidon, and the desert march depended on water skins, camel trains and a limited number of wells, which is precisely why Antigonus had to take Gaza first as a supply base.
tactics: 這場戰爭可以分成四段。第一段是進軍與沙漠遭遇：安提柯先在敘利亞與腓尼基集結，沿海路南下，繞開或橫穿西奈半島的旱地，進入阿拉伯邊境；希臘史料提到的「舊門」（Παλαιὰ πύλη）是這支軍隊深入內陸的標誌，那是一處峽口式隘道，位置到今天仍無法確定。安提柯的目標顯然是納巴泰人的商路節點，而納巴泰人靠熟悉水源的駱駝隊與輕騎在沙地裡周旋；摘要記載安提柯在內陸遭到挫敗，被追到幾乎無法脫身，損失慘重到沒有留下可核對的數字。第二段是改攻加沙：既然在沙漠裡追不上對手，安提柯便回頭攻取加沙這座海陸商運的終點，用封鎖港池、圍城斷糧的辦法把它拿下。第三段是聯軍前來解圍：托勒密與塞琉古合兵，連同安提柯的兒子德米特里一起北上，在加沙附近的平原上與安提柯接戰。史料描述聯軍列陣時步兵居中、兩翼各有騎兵，兩軍先以騎兵互相衝撞；安提柯把自己的騎兵集中起來打聯軍的騎兵翼，聯軍騎兵潰散，追擊成為安提柯主動出擊的契機。第四段是方陣對撞：安提柯的方陣在正面頂住了聯軍重裝步兵的衝擊，並在某一翼一度吃緊，靠騎兵及時迴援與方陣的縱深才沒有被衝垮；聯軍的方陣一旦被帶亂就再也無法重整，全軍退向埃及與東方。同一份摘要還記下了一句最著名的技術對比：一方是「密集而輕裝」，另一方是「重裝而稀疏」——勝負就在這兩種配置的差別上。這種「方陣正面加騎兵側翼衝擊」的組合，是安提柯此後十年反覆使用的模式，也在他公元前301年伊普索斯會戰中走到盡頭。
tacticsEn: This war can be divided into four stages. The first is the advance and the encounter in the desert: Antigonus first mustered in Syria and Phoenicia, moved south along the coast, skirted or crossed the dry country of the Sinai, and entered the Arabian frontier; the Old Gates that the Greek sources mention mark how far inland this army went, a defile-like pass whose position cannot be fixed to this day. Antigonus's object was plainly a node of the Nabataean trade route, while the Nabataeans moved about the sand with camel trains and light cavalry that knew the waterholes; the summary records that Antigonus was worsted in the interior, pressed to the point of near-flight, and so badly mauled that no verifiable figure survives. The second stage is the change of plan to Gaza: unable to run his quarry down in the desert, Antigonus turned back and attacked Gaza, the terminus of the trade that ran by sea and land, and took it by sealing the harbour and besieging the city until it starved. The third stage is the relief of Gaza: Ptolemy and Seleucus joined their forces and, with Antigonus's son Demetrius, marched north and engaged Antigonus on the plain near Gaza. The sources describe the coalition deploying with infantry in the centre and cavalry on either flank, the two sides first colliding with their horse, Antigonus massing his cavalry against that of the coalition, which broke and scattered, and the pursuit becoming the opening for Antigonus's own attack. The fourth stage is the collision of the phalanxes: Antigonus's phalanx absorbed the shock of the coalition's heavy infantry in the centre and was pressed hard on one wing, saved from being broken by cavalry returning in time and by the depth of the formation, and the coalition's phalanx, once disordered, could never be reformed; the whole allied army fell back towards Egypt and the East. The same summary preserves the most famous technical contrast of the day: on one side a phalanx that was dense and lightly equipped, on the other one that was heavily equipped and sparse, and the whole issue lay in the difference between those two configurations. The combination of a phalanx in the centre and a cavalry blow on the flank was the pattern Antigonus used again and again for the following ten years, and it was carried to its end at Ipsus in 301 BC.
data: 這場戰爭沒有留下任何可核對的當代數字，唯一詳細的敘述來自狄奧多羅斯《史學》第十五卷，而該卷本身只剩費提烏斯的摘要與辛刻魯斯的引錄，晚出四個多世紀。可引用的數字大致是這些：安提柯解圍軍的兵力，傳統記載為約九千步兵與四千騎兵；聯軍方面，托勒密、塞琉古與德米特里的合計兵力常被讀作二萬上下步兵與數千騎兵，但同一份摘要也說聯軍的騎兵在正式接戰前就已望風而散，因此任何數字都只能當作約數，甚至當作誇張來看。安提柯在沙漠中損失的人數，摘要只說慘重而不給數字，這一點值得記下。時間方面：公元前312年是通行採用的年份；月份在史料中沒有定論，本卡採用年末（十二月）一說，理由是加沙會戰之後塞琉古返回東方重建勢力，而塞琉古王朝的紀年正是以公元前312/311年為元年。地理方面：加沙在古代是離海約數公里的內陸港城，城牆線周長在數公里之內；由加沙深入阿拉伯內陸的「舊門」地帶沒有可考的里程，學界只能指出它應在西奈半島東南部或阿拉伯邊疆一帶。戰果數字則完全沒有留下：安提柯軍、聯軍與納巴泰人的損耗，史料都只作敘述而不作計數。
dataEn: This war leaves behind no verifiable contemporary figures. The only detailed narrative comes from Diodorus, History of the Fifteenth Book, and that book survives only in the epitome of Photius and in excerpts of Syncellus, four centuries and more after the event. The numbers that can be quoted are roughly these: the strength of Antigonus's relieving force is traditionally given as about nine thousand foot and four thousand horse; on the coalition side, the combined force of Ptolemy, Seleucus and Demetrius is usually read as some twenty thousand foot and several thousand horse, though the same summary also says that the allied horse scattered before the fighting was joined, so that any such figure must be treated as an approximation, or even as an exaggeration. The number Antigonus lost in the desert is given only as heavy, without a count, and that is worth setting down. As to time: 312 BC is the year in general use; the month is not fixed by the sources, and this card adopts the end of the year, December, on the ground that after the battle of Gaza Seleucus returned east to rebuild his position, and the Seleucid era is counted from 312/311 BC. As to geography: Gaza in antiquity was an inland port city lying some kilometres from the sea, and the line of its walls ran for a matter of a few kilometres; the country of the Old Gates deep in the Arabian interior has no measurable distance attached to it, and scholarship can only say that it must have lain in the south-east of the Sinai or on the Arabian frontier. As to the results of the fighting, no figures at all survive: the losses of Antigonus's army, of the coalition and of the Nabataeans are described but never counted.
cause: 要打起來，理由分幾層。最表層是商路：安提柯要的是從阿拉伯到地中海的香料與乳香貿易，納巴泰人控制這條線的沙漠段與加沙的終點，兩邊的利害直接撞在一起。安提柯更深的一層目標，是把地中海東岸連成一體——他已握有呂基亞、弗里吉亞、敘利亞、腓尼基與小亞細亞東岸，剩下的空缺就是阿拉伯邊界，而加沙是填上這個空缺的鑰匙。托勒密與塞琉古的介入則是另一種算盤：公元前312年春天，安提柯的兒子德米特里在塞浦路斯薩拉米斯海戰中擊潰托勒密的艦隊，俘虜了托勒密的兄弟梅涅勞斯與羅得島的阿拉托斯；托勒密急需一場勝利來穩住埃及，塞琉古則在東方剛被逐出，亟需能鼓舞自己陣營的消息，兩人因此走到一起，聯軍北上解加沙之圍。納巴泰一方不需要宣戰的理由：安提柯的軍隊帶著攻城器械進入他們的腹地，等於要終結沙漠商路上的獨立性，他們的抵抗是自保。技術層面的原因更實在：安提柯的方陣與騎兵依賴穩定的糧食與水，沙漠行軍最缺的就是水，因此他必須先拿下一座可以靠海運補給的城市，這就把一場野戰拖成了圍城戰。底層則是帝國崩解後的無政府狀態：亞歷山大沒有指定繼承者，所有繼業者都以「亞歷山大的繼承者」自居，彼此兼併的理由寫在每一份公告與每一封致土邦的信裡。
causeEn: The reasons for going to war lie in several layers. The outermost is the trade route: Antigonus wanted the spice and incense trade that ran from Arabia to the Mediterranean, the Nabataeans controlled the desert stretch of that line and its terminus at Gaza, and the interests of the two sides collided directly. A layer deeper for Antigonus was the wish to join up the eastern Mediterranean coast into one: he already held Lycia, Phrygia, Syria, Phoenicia and the east coast of Asia Minor, and the one gap left was the Arabian frontier, with Gaza as the key that would fill it. The intervention of Ptolemy and Seleucus was a different calculation. In the spring of 312 BC Antigonus's son Demetrius had beaten Ptolemy's fleet in the naval battle of Salamis in Cyprus, taking Ptolemy's brother Menelaus and the Rhodian Aratus prisoner; Ptolemy badly needed a victory to hold Egypt together, and Seleucus, freshly driven out of the East, needed news that would hearten his own side, so the two joined hands and marched north to relieve Gaza. The Nabataeans needed no declared grievance: an army with siege equipment entering their interior meant an end to the independence of the desert roads, and their resistance was self-preservation. The technical reasons are blunter still. Antigonus's phalanx and horse depended on steady grain and water, and water is what a march across the desert most lacks, so he had to take a city that could be supplied by sea, and that is what turned a field campaign into a siege. At the bottom lies the lawlessness that followed the empire's collapse: Alexander appointed no successor, every one of the successors called himself the successor of Alexander, and the grounds for swallowing a neighbour were written into every proclamation and every letter to the cities.
impact: 這場戰爭的影響，短的看是兩個政權命運的分岔，長的看是地中海東岸格局的定型。第一，托勒密退回埃及，此後再沒有在陸上成功挑戰安提柯系，他把精力轉向埃及本國的制度與神廟經營，托勒密王朝的穩固期由此開始。塞琉古帶著敗訊回到東方，卻在東方取得了比在西方更大的收穫：塞琉古王朝的紀年由此起算，安提柯的勢力退到小亞細亞與敘利亞一線，亞洲的權力版圖自此固定下來，而安提柯此後再也沒有回來。第二，安提柯贏了這場會戰，卻被釘死在黎凡特：西線的卡山德得以在歐洲鞏固，公元前301年伊普索斯的敗績，正是他長期無法兼顧東西的結果。第三，軍事技術上，這是「方陣加騎兵」制勝模式的一次早期示範。安提柯在戰後十年裡把方陣改造得更輕、更長、更整齊，把希臘式頭盔、小圓盾與加長長矛編入前排，形成安提柯方陣的樣子；這套裝備在伊普索斯會戰中既救不了他，也確實是最終逼死他的東西。第四，納巴泰人退向阿拉伯半島南部，轉而在東方與安條克人、塞琉古人角力，並在兩百多年後的馬其頓衰落期成為地中海東岸的強者。第五，這場戰爭在古典世界並不常被獨立講述，它多半以「加沙會戰」之名附在繼業者戰爭的總述之下；但就兵器史而言，把科林斯盔放在這裡是有意義的：它記錄了一頂頭盔從城邦重裝步兵的舊制裝備，走向帝國方陣標準配備的那條路。
impactEn: The consequences of this war are, in the short run, a divergence in the fortunes of two states, and in the long run, the fixing of the shape of the eastern Mediterranean. First, Ptolemy fell back into Egypt and never again challenged the Antigonid line on land; he turned his energy to the institutions and temples of Egypt itself, and the settled period of the Ptolemaic dynasty begins here. Seleucus went home to the East with the news of a defeat, and won in the East far more than he had lost in the West: the Seleucid era is counted from this point, Antigonus's power is pushed back to the line of Asia Minor and Syria, the map of authority in Asia is fixed from here on, and Antigonus never came back. Second, Antigonus won the field engagement but was nailed down to the Levant: Cassander was left free to consolidate in Europe, and the defeat at Ipsus in 301 BC is the direct result of an inability to hold both ends of his front at once. Third, in military technology this is an early demonstration of the winning formula of phalanx plus cavalry. In the ten years after the battle Antigonus lightened his phalanx, lengthened it, made it neater, and built the Greek-style helmet, the small round shield and the lengthened spear into the front ranks, so that the Antigonid phalanx acquired its final form; that equipment saved Antigonus nothing at Ipsus, and it was precisely what killed him. Fourth, the Nabataeans withdrew deeper into southern Arabia, turned to contest the East with the Antiochus line and with the Seleucids, and became the great power of the eastern Mediterranean two centuries later, as Macedon declined. Fifth, in the classical world this war is seldom told on its own; it usually hangs from the general account of the wars of the successors under the name of the battle of Gaza. In the history of arms, however, setting the Corinthian helmet here is meaningful, for it records the path by which a helmet moved from being the old equipment of the heavy infantry of the city-states to being the standard kit of an imperial phalanx.
result: 打完之後，加沙連同周邊的阿拉伯邊境歸入安提柯之手，納巴泰人的商隊被迫繞道或改走更南的路線；前來解圍的聯軍在加沙附近的會戰中被擊潰，各部退回埃及與東方。兩年之後托勒密在加沙城下捲土重來，攻守之勢再度逆轉，公元前306年安提柯在那一戰中失去右眼，從此得了「獨眼」的綽號，隨即在戰敗與丟失腓尼基港口之後退向亞細亞。可以這樣總結：安提柯贏了這場會戰，卻把最難打的對手留給了未來——他既沒有真正消滅納巴泰人，也沒有真正困住托勒密，沙漠的邊界與地中海的港口都只是暫時換了主人。安提柯本人又活了十年，終於在前301年的伊普索斯會戰中，把這裡贏來的方陣戰法用到盡頭，也把性命輸掉。整個事件在東方的編年史上被視為塞琉古時代的起點：正是這場戰役之後，塞琉古回到巴比倫重建王國，而安提柯在亞洲的霸權從此有了確切的起算年份。
resultEn: When the fighting was over, Gaza and the Arabian frontier around it had fallen to Antigonus, and the Nabataean caravans were forced to detour or to take a route further south. The relief force was broken in the engagement near Gaza, and its several contingents fell back towards Egypt and the East. Two years later Ptolemy came back to Gaza and turned the tables once more; in 306 BC Antigonus lost his right eye in that battle, won the nickname of the One-Eyed, and then, after the defeat and the loss of the Phoenician ports, withdrew towards Asia. The result can be put this way: Antigonus won the field engagement but left his hardest opponents for later. He destroyed neither the Nabataeans nor truly penned in Ptolemy; the desert frontier and the Mediterranean port had merely changed hands for a while. Antigonus himself lived another ten years and at last, at Ipsus in 301 BC, carried the phalanx method won here to its limit and lost his life with it. In the chronicles of the East the whole affair is treated as the beginning of the Seleucid era: it was after this campaign that Seleucus returned to Babylon and rebuilt his kingdom, and from this point the Antigonid hegemony in Asia has a precise starting date.
